Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

**Please check your phone's status bar (the strip at the very top of the screen) and tell me everything you see**, specifically whether any of these appear:

turns.thought:
You found it — and you're right, that explains the complete "No Connection." Both of these will block data independently, so let's clear them one at a time so we can tell which is which.

**Step 1 — Turn Airplane Mode OFF**

Airplane Mode is the big one: it disables **all** of your phone's wireless radios — cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. While it's on, no amount of data on your plan can reach your phone. That alone fully accounts for a dead connection.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet** (or **Connections**, depending on your phone), and toggle **Airplane mode** to **OFF**.
- On many phones you can also swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings and tap the **✈️** tile to switch it off.

**Step 2 — Tell me what the status bar shows afterward**

This is the important part, so please look again before we move on:
- Do you now see a **signal strength** indicator (📶 with bars) instead of 📵 No Signal?
- Do you see a **network type** like **5G, 4G, or LTE**?
- Do you see **📱 Data Enabled**?

**About the VPN — let's leave it on for now.** I know it's tempting to switch off both, and we very likely will disconnect it. But a VPN can only work *if* there's an underlying data connection, and right now we don't know whether one exists. If I have you disable it at the same time as Airplane Mode, and data then works, we won't know which change fixed it — and if it *doesn't* work, we won't know which one is still to blame. Doing this in order keeps the diagnosis clean.

Once you've got a signal with Airplane Mode off, we'll test the speed again with the VPN still connected. If it's slow or still dead at that point, the VPN becomes the prime suspect and we'll disconnect it then — a misconfigured or congested VPN is a classic cause of crawling speeds even when the cellular connection itself is healthy.

Go ahead and turn Airplane Mode off, then let me know exactly what's showing in the status bar.

turns.thought:
Excellent progress — we've confirmed real information here. Airplane Mode was indeed blocking you, and now we can see the connection underneath. You actually have **three** separate things going on, and we'll clear them one at a time, in order of what's blocking you hardest right now.

**Step 1 — Turn Mobile Data ON** (do this now)

This is the hard blocker at the moment. Your plan data and your 2 GB refuel are both sitting there unused because the phone's main Mobile Data switch is off — that's exactly the "📵 Data Disabled" you're seeing, and it produces a dead connection just like Airplane Mode did.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network** and toggle **Mobile data** to **ON**.
- Or swipe down to Quick Settings and tap the mobile data / signal tile to enable it.

Then run the speed test again and tell me the result.

**What we already know about the other two — so you know what's coming:**

**The 2G network is a real problem and we will fix it.** 2G is an ancient data technology — even with data enabled, it will crawl or fail outright. It's also too slow for picture/video messaging. Once data is on, I'll have you change your **network mode preference** to prefer 4G/5G, which should make a dramatic difference. I want to do this *after* enabling data so we can measure each fix separately rather than changing three things at once and guessing which one worked.

**The VPN is still connected, and it's still a suspect.** A misconfigured or congested VPN can throttle you to a crawl even on a perfectly good cellular connection. Since we don't yet know whether a working underlying connection exists, I'm keeping it on for one more round — if your speed test comes back slow or dead once data is on, the VPN moves to the top of the list and we'll disconnect it right away.

One caveat worth setting in advance: your signal is showing **📶¹ Poor**. Signal strength is largely about your physical location — where you are relative to a tower. Changing settings can help your phone use the *best available* network, and moving to 4G/5G often feels much better even at one bar, but if you're in a basement, a thick-walled building, or a rural spot, some slowness may simply be environmental. Moving near a window or outdoors often helps. We'll see what the numbers say after these fixes.

Go ahead and enable Mobile Data, run the speed test, and tell me what you get.

Good — that's still useful information, not a dead end. Data Enabled means the switch worked; the "No Connection" now has to be coming from something else, and you've handed me the next clue yourself: **Data Saver just appeared.**

**Step 1 — Turn Data Saver OFF** (do this now)

Data Saver is the top suspect for the current state. It restricts background data and throttles throughput to conserve data, and it can absolutely produce a dead-or-crawling result exactly like what you're seeing.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver** (sometimes called **Data Saver** or **Data Warning & limit**) and turn it **OFF**.

**Here's the key piece of context: turning Data Saver off is likely what lets your 2 GB refuel actually take effect.** While Data Saver is on, the phone is deliberately clamping down on data use — so the data I added to your account may be effectively held back at the device level regardless of the plan allowance. Clearing it removes that clamp.

**Step 2 — Then change off 2G** (right after)

Do this once Data Saver is off. Your phone is camped on **2G**, which is a legacy network — far too slow for real data use, and too slow for picture/video messaging. Even with everything else correct, 2G alone can look like no connection.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Preferred network mode** (may be called **Network mode**).
- Change it from 2G to the highest available option — **5G/4G preferred** or **LTE/4G**, whichever your phone offers.

**Then run the speed test again and tell me the result.**

I'm deliberately holding the VPN off the list for one more round. A VPN can only throttle traffic if there's an underlying connection to route — and right now we still haven't confirmed one exists. Once we've cleared Data Saver and the 2G lock, you'll either have data (in which case we know it wasn't the network) or you won't. Either way, the VPN is our clean final suspect and we'll disconnect it next if needed.

One honest note about your signal: **📶¹ Poor** is your one remaining environmental limit. Moving to 4G/5G usually feels dramatically better even at a single bar, and moving near a window or outdoors can help — but if you're somewhere with genuinely weak coverage, some slowness may persist no matter what we change. Go ahead with Data Saver first, then 2G, then the speed test.

turns.thought:
Yes — disconnect the VPN now. That's the right call, and you've earned it by working through everything else.

**Here's why this is now the strongest lead:** your signal went from 📶¹ Poor/2G to **excellent 5G**. That's a real, meaningful win — it confirms the cellular connection itself is alive and healthy, and that turning off Data Saver and moving off 2G genuinely worked. When the network is good but data still reports nothing, and a VPN is sitting in the path, the VPN becomes the prime suspect by elimination. A VPN that's misconfigured, expired, or connected to a dead server can black-hole all traffic even on a perfect 5G connection.

**How to disconnect it:**
- Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings, then tap the **🔒 VPN** tile to disconnect.
- Or go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN**, tap the connected VPN, and select **Disconnect / Forget**.

**Then — and this part matters:** after disconnecting, **restart your phone completely** (hold the power button, then tap Restart). Your phone has had Airplane Mode, Mobile Data, Data Saver, and network mode all changed in quick succession, and a reboot clears out any stale connection state left over from the VPN session. Plenty of data issues resolve only after that fresh start.

Once it's back up, run the speed test again and tell me what you get.

**If it still shows "No Connection" after the reboot**, we have two solid checks left, so this is far from over:
1. **APN settings** — these tell your phone how to reach the carrier's data network. If they're incorrect or missing, you'll have full bars and zero data, which matches your symptoms uncomfortably well. I'd have you reset them to default and reboot again.
2. **SIM status** — I'd confirm the SIM is reading as Active; a reseat can fix recognition problems.

For what it's worth: you've gone from no signal at all on 2G to excellent 5G in the course of this conversation. That's real progress, and it means the network side is genuinely fixed — whatever is left is a settings issue on the device, and those are all solvable. Go ahead and disconnect the VPN, reboot, and let me know.

turns.thought:
You have every right to be frustrated — you've done a lot of work here, and I want to acknowledge the genuinely good part first: **your status bar is now showing 📶⁴ Excellent on 5G with data enabled.** That's a completely different picture from where we started (no signal, 2G, airplane mode on). The network connection itself is solid. So we're no longer chasing a broken connection — we're chasing why the phone isn't *using* it.

That narrows things to two settings-level causes, and you named them exactly. Let's take them in order.

**Step 1 — Check your APN settings** (start here; it's the more likely of the two)

APN settings tell your phone how to reach the carrier's data network. A phone can show full 5G bars and still pass zero data if these are wrong — which matches your symptoms precisely.

- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Access Point Names** (on some phones: **Mobile networks → Access Point Names**).
- Look at the APN that is selected, and tell me:
  - Is there an **APN name** listed, and is it flagged as incorrect or empty?
  - Is there an **MMSC** field, and does it have a URL in it?

**If the APN shows anything incorrect, or the MMSC is empty** → use the **Reset to default** option (usually the ⋮ three-dot menu → *Reset to default*). Then **restart your phone**, because APN changes don't take effect until after a reboot.

**Step 2 — Check your SIM status**

- Go to **Settings → About phone → Status → SIM status** (or **Settings → Network & Internet → SIMs**).
- Tell me what it says: **Active**, **Missing / No SIM**, or **Locked**.

Here's how we'll handle each:
- **Active** → the SIM is fine, and the APN is almost certainly our culprit.
- **Missing / No SIM** → I'll walk you through removing and reinserting the SIM card; a poorly seated SIM commonly causes exactly this "bars but no data" pattern. Given your line had a SIM replacement recorded earlier this year, this is well worth ruling out.
- **Locked (PIN/PUK)** → I can't unlock that for you, and I'll transfer you to technical support for SIM security help.

Report back what you see on those two screens and I'll tell you the next move.

**And one clear offer:** if you'd rather not keep hunting through phone menus — completely understandable after all this — say the word and I'll transfer you to a human agent with a full summary of everything we've done, so they can pick straight up from the APN/SIM stage without you repeating yourself. Your call, and there's no downside to choosing it.
